0.text: Silver ETFs versus physical silver: The tax difference is everything.

1.text: Both physical silver and silver ETFs like SLV get taxed at the same federal long-term capital gains rate of up to 28 percent
because the IRS classifies both as collectibles.
That is the headline most investors miss.
The real differences live in short-term treatment, state sales tax, dealer reporting thresholds
and what happens when you actually sell.

2.text: When you sell SLV shares held longer than one year
your gain hits a maximum federal rate of 28 percent
the same ceiling that applies to a tube of Silver Eagles in your safe.

3.text: A buyer in the 32 percent bracket owes $480.
A buyer in the 12 percent bracket owes $180.
The lesson is simple: silver is a position, not a trade.
Hold past the one-year mark or expect to give back a third of your profit.

4.text: Physical silver has zero phantom basis adjustments.
Your basis is what you paid, period.
Physical sales above certain thresholds trigger a 1099-B.
